body: No sensitive data should traverse through HTTP protocol. I think this requirement (8.3.1) reads as if it was allowed in the body or headers of the request.

comments.body: That is interesting. Please can you raise a pull request with the suggested change. Is there anywhere else in the standard that this exists?

commit 335b612

There is no such thing like HTTP**S** message body (it's HTTP message body). HTTPS is just extended HTTP. Like HTTP header is not HTTPS header just because HTTPS protocol was used.

https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.3
Then the requirement 8.3.1 should read as "Verify that sensitive data is NOT sent to the server in the HTTP message body or headers..."

If it can not be sent in HTTP message body or headers, it means, it can not be sent at all. The point for 8.3.1 is that sensitive data can not be sent in part of URL request or parameter part (path or query part, https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-3), because those are often present in logs, in browser history, referrer problems etc.

For me requirement V8.3.1 is understandable and clear.
Agree with you on the URL request parameters, but the HTTP BODY (which is mentioned in 8.3.1) is causing the confusion.

It's "HTTP message body", not "HTTP BODY", and it should be clear term for every security tester and web developer.

HTTP request
```
POST /path/no-sensitive-data-here/?parameter=no-sensitive-data-here HTTP/1.1
User-Agent: ...
Another-Header: sensitive-data-allowed

message-body-is-here=sensitive-data-allowed
```

Absolutely correct. The terms "HTTP Message Body" or "Message Body" are 
standard where "HTTP Body" is not.

- Jim

The current version I'm reading says:

"Verify that sensitive data is sent to the server in the HTTP message 
body or headers, and that query string parameters from any HTTP verb do 
not contain sensitive data."

This looks very clear to me. If anyone objects can you please suggest an 
exact replacement?

The principle to NOT put sensitive data in a querystring of any verb, 
even over HTTPS, is one of the core principles of secure web development 
and it's a solid and critical requirement.

Ravi, we do NOT want to send sensitive data in the querystring and we 
WANT to send sensitive data ONLY in a HTTP header or HTTP message body. 
And of course we want to use HTTP/S but that is a different requirement.

So the current requirement 8.3.1 is still quite reasonable.

- Jim
